subject: psychology
title: Memory: Models of Memory
welcome_lead: From sensory flicker to lifetime store — meet the architecture of memory.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology memory models: MSM Atkinson & Shiffrin 1968, WMM Baddeley & Hitch 1974.
final_note: Models are scaffolds; remember which evidence each can and cannot carry.

concepts.def: Multi-Store Model — sensory register, STM, LTM in a linear chain.
Working Memory Model — STM as multiple active components.
Short-term memory — limited capacity, acoustic encoding, ~18s duration.
Long-term memory — vast capacity, semantic encoding, potentially lifelong.
Attention controller of the WMM directing slave systems.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Multi-Store Model proposes information flows from sensory register to STM via attention, and from STM to LTM via rehearsal. STM holds 7±2 items (Miller 1956) for ~18s (Peterson & Peterson 1959); LTM is potentially lifelong (Bahrick 1975).

The Working Memory Model replaces unitary STM with a central executive, phonological loop, visuo-spatial sketchpad and (added in 2000) an episodic buffer. Each slave system has its own modality-specific capacity.

Dual-task studies (Baddeley & Hitch) show two visual tasks compete but visual + verbal do not — supporting WMM, not MSM. Case study KF (Shallice & Warrington 1970) had damaged verbal STM but intact visual STM, again showing STM is not unitary.
